response.sql: WITH s AS (SELECT p.death_state, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM hall_of_fame h JOIN player p ON p.player_id = h.player_id GROUP BY p.death_state), a AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_all FROM s), k AS (SELECT s.cnt, a.avg_all FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.cnt > a.avg_all) SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_count, AVG(cnt - avg_all) AS avg_excess FROM k

assumptions.assumption: Players with NULL death_state (e.g., still living or unknown) form one group, and that group is included in the average across states. GROUP BY puts NULLs in one group, as the request specifies.
The 'average count across states' is the unweighted mean of per-state counts, including the NULL group, computed over all groups before filtering.
Empty-string death_state values, if any, are treated as their own distinct state group, separate from NULL.
